articles.title: FIGMA BRINGS ITS AGENT TO DEV MODE FOR DESIGN HANDOFFS
articles.summary: Figma's agent now works inside Dev Mode, answering design questions, comparing versions, and preparing code snippets and asset download links. Dev seats can chat without changing a design, while Full seats with edit access can also request edits. Dev Mode is unavailable on Starter plans, and agent usage consumes AI credits based on task complexity.

articles.title: BING TESTS A HOMEPAGE SEARCH BAR REDESIGN WITH A “WHAT'S ON YOUR MIND?” PROMPT
articles.summary: Microsoft is testing a redesigned Bing homepage search bar that replaces the traditional "Search the web" placeholder with the more conversational "What's on your mind?" prompt. The interface introduces a dedicated web search button and reorganizes the plus menu into separate Attach and Tools sections, with options for adding images and generating them. The changes bring Bing closer to an AI chatbot experience while preserving conventional search functionality, although the scope of the experiment remains unclear.

articles.title: WHY HAS NORTH KOREA REDESIGNED ITS FLAG? IT'S NOT ABOUT AESTHETICS...
articles.summary: North Korea has changed its national flag's proportions from 1:2 to 1:1.65, thickening the white stripes and shifting the star closer to the center. The move may reflect its increasingly explicit rejection of reunification with South Korea rather than a purely aesthetic redesign.

articles.title: DESIGN TOOLS JUST GOT PERSONAL
articles.summary: Building your own tools is part of the design job again. In the UX Tools prototyping survey, 59% of 1,478 respondents had built a tool of their own with AI in the previous six months. Those tools encode a designer's judgment and way of working, making them more worth showing in a portfolio than finished screens.

articles.title: THE ATTACK OF THE GIANT AI DESIGN SLOP MONSTER: A SURVIVOR'S GUIDE
articles.summary: AI coding tools allow product managers, developers, and designers to create convincing interfaces quickly, but the results can introduce usability problems, inconsistent patterns, and technical risks that designers must subsequently resolve. When AI-generated prototypes become implementation requirements without proper validation, design teams risk spending more time repairing flawed decisions than they would have spent designing the experience correctly. Establishing explicit guardrails for user research, design systems, accessibility, and security can help teams use AI effectively while maintaining responsibility for the quality of the resulting products.

articles.title: WHY AI FACTORIES NEED A DESIGN SYSTEM
articles.summary: AI agents generating websites and interfaces need shared design rules to prevent inconsistent components, inaccessible experiences, and repeated human corrections. Kirupa's ROFL design system provides machine-readable tokens, component specifications, layouts, accessibility requirements, and task-specific instructions that agents can consult before building. Automated source checks help verify generated work against the system. Browser-based checks are still needed across its nine visual styles in light and dark modes, while human reviewers focus on decisions that require judgment rather than correcting predictable mistakes.

articles.title: FIGMA PROTOTYPE USABILITY TESTING: HOW TO TEST WITH USERS BEFORE YOU BUILD
articles.summary: Testing a Figma prototype with users before engineering builds it turns review debates about taste into evidence: task success, time on task, paths, and recordings. Fair results depend on linking every screen a task needs, sharing a login-free link, and writing tasks as goals rather than click paths. Rerunning the same tasks on the live site later yields a comparable before-and-after baseline.

articles.title: HOCHBURG BRINGS TOGETHER PIZZA AND HIP-HOP IN L'ARTISTA'S IDENTITY
articles.summary: Stuttgart-based Hochburg has created a distinctive identity for Neapolitan pizza brand L'Artista, combining traditional pizza-making with the visual energy of hip-hop, vintage MTV graphics, and New York street culture. The system centers on a hand-drawn wordmark with multiple variations that change shape and proportion, supported by bold Rekind Expanded typography, Ivar Mono, and expressive motion graphics. Oversized lettering extends across pizza boxes, menus, merchandise, and restaurant interiors, giving L'Artista an identity that feels closer to an independent hip-hop label than a conventional pizzeria.

articles.title: VERVE CASTS LEGACY SOFTWARE AS THE STONE AGE IN REBRAND FOR AI STARTUP ZERO
articles.summary: Amsterdam-based Verve has rebranded Helsinki AI startup Zero, positioning its software as an evolutionary leap that could make traditional customer relationship management platforms obsolete. The identity depicts legacy CRM systems as a prehistoric landscape of cracked earth and fossilized tools, contrasted with Zero's futuristic, alien-inspired technology and a character named Zorb. Designed as both a brand identity and an expandable campaign platform, the system combines unconventional creative concepts with AI-assisted production to support future marketing, events, and product communications.

articles.title: ADOBE'S DEMOCRATIZATION OF DESIGN DOESN'T HAVE TO BE THE DEATH OF HUMAN CREATIVITY
articles.summary: Adobe MAX 2026 made clear that Adobe pitches its tools at everyone, from novices to industry veterans, deepening worries about AI slop and the value of craft.

articles.summary: Philadelphia agency Creative Repute runs every UX/UI project through the same six-step, research-driven process, from discovery and Figma wireframes to prototyping, build, launch, and support.
